trial_court: Family Court, Secunderabad (Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.797/03)
case_name: K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa — Civil Appeal No. 1794 of 2013
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 1999 but separated without consummation on the next day due to disputes between their elders. The respondent-wife filed a complaint against the appellant-husband for dowry harassment and he filed a counter-claim seeking divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion. The Family Court granted decree of divorce to the husband.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty can be caused by a sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment.
legal_principles.held: A sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment calculated to torture, discommode or render miserable life of the spouse.
cited_cases: V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat (1994) 1 SCC 337

legal_principles.principle: The married life should be reviewed as a whole, and a few isolated instances over a period of years will not amount to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The ill conduct must be persistent for a fairly lengthy period, where the relationship has deteriorated to an extent that because of the acts and behaviour of a spouse, the wronged party finds it extremely difficult to live with the other party any longer, may amount to mental cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The treatment complained of and the resultant danger or apprehension must be very grave, substantial and weighty.
legal_principles.held: Sustained unjustifiable conduct and behaviour of one spouse actually affecting physical and mental health of the other spouse. The treatment complained of and the resultant danger or apprehension must be very grave, substantial and weighty.

outcome.final_order: The Supreme Court set aside the judgment of the High Court and restored the decree of divorce granted by the Family Court.

use_for_drafting: assisting in separation and non-consummation matters
